sections.html:
Eagle Mountain is a city in northwest Utah County, in the flat Cedar Valley west and north of the Lake Mountains, and it belongs to the Provo-Orem metropolitan area. It covers about 50 square miles at an elevation of roughly 4,885 feet, which makes it one of the larger cities by area on the Wasatch Front.

Because the city is in Utah County, your tax bill, deed recording and property records all run through Provo, the county seat. Utah County's treasurer and recorder are both in the county building at 100 East Center Street.

sections.h2: How did Eagle Mountain become a city so quickly?
sections.html:
In 1994 three investors bought about 8,000 acres at a bankruptcy auction in western Utah County, and on December 3, 1996 the area incorporated as the Town of Eagle Mountain. It was renamed Eagle Mountain City in 2001, and in 2011 it annexed the White Hills neighborhood and nearly 2,900 acres.

The census numbers show how fast it moved.

  • 2000: 2,157 residents
  • 2010: 21,415 residents
  • 2020: 43,623 residents
  • July 1, 2025: an estimated 66,557 residents (Census Bureau)

The city still holds traces of older history, including a site on the original Pony Express trail and a boulder with petroglyphs carved by the Fremont people about 1,800 years ago.

sections.h2: What drives the Eagle Mountain economy?
sections.html:
Data centers are the most visible employer. Meta broke ground on its Eagle Mountain campus in 2018, began operations in 2021 and, in September 2026, confirmed a further expansion that brings its Utah investment above $3 billion. The company says construction will peak at about 1,200 jobs and that more than 300 permanent roles will follow, though those are company figures.

QTS and Google also have data center operations or plans here, and the developer Tract bought 668 acres in 2024 for future campuses. A 150-megawatt battery storage project is expected online later in 2026.

For a house seller, the point is that demand for local workers, contractors and housing has a large industrial anchor. Meta also projects that it will become one of the city's largest property taxpayers, which could eventually ease pressure on residential tax rates, although no rate change has been announced.

The 2020 census found a median age of 22.4 and 44.7% of residents under 18. A household size of 4.18 is among the largest of any Wasatch Front city we have researched, and the owner-occupied rate of 84.7% means very few homes are rentals.

sections.h2: Which school district serves Eagle Mountain?
sections.html:
Today the Alpine School District serves Eagle Mountain, but that changes on July 1, 2027, when the district splits into three. Eagle Mountain, Saratoga Springs, Cedar Fort and Fairfield will form the Lake Mountain School District, while Lehi, American Fork, Highland, Alpine and Cedar Hills go to Aspen Peaks and Orem, Pleasant Grove, Lindon and Vineyard go to Timpanogos.

Current schools include eight elementary schools, Frontier Middle School and Cedar Valley High School, which opened in August 2019, along with charter schools such as The Ranches Academy, John Hancock Charter School and Rockwell Charter High School. If you are selling during the transition, expect buyers to ask which district the address will land in, and send them to the district office for current boundary maps.

sections.h2: How do roads and climate shape life in Eagle Mountain?
sections.html:
The main routes are SR-73, Pony Express Parkway, Eagle Mountain Boulevard and Ranches Parkway. The Mountain View Corridor segment linking the Salt Lake and Utah valleys was completed in December 2025, and UTA has run express bus Route 806 since 2008.

Rainfall is light. The Ranches area averages about 16.75 inches of precipitation a year, and the city center is drier, cooler and has colder nights, with a combined average July high of 90 degrees. A low-rainfall, high-sun climate is hard on roofing, wood fences and stucco, so ask for a roof age and last inspection date when you prepare to sell.

sections.h2: What are Eagle Mountain's rules for accessory units and short-term rentals?
sections.html:
Eagle Mountain allows accessory dwelling units, but not in townhomes, duplexes or apartments, and an ADU permit is required in addition to any building permit.

  • The unit needs its own kitchen, bathroom and separate entrance.
  • The owner must live in either the main home or the ADU, with temporary absences allowed.
  • The site plan must show two off-street parking spaces.
  • The application fee is $230.
  • ADUs cannot be rented for fewer than 30 consecutive days.

Unpermitted units are treated as illegal until an application is approved. Short-term rentals of any kind also carry a 1% transient room tax under city code, with records kept for at least three years. Unpaid amounts add a 10% penalty and 12% annual interest, and the operator's business license can be revoked.

sections.h2: How are property taxes and deed recording handled in Eagle Mountain?
sections.html:
Utah County sets the dates: the Auditor mails valuation notices around July 22, Board of Equalization appeals are due September 1, tax notices go out in the third week of October, and real property taxes are due November 30. Mailed payments count if they carry a U.S. Post Office postmark, but a postage meter mark from an office does not.

On December 1, delinquent parcels are charged the greater of $10 or 1%. Utah residents also get the state's 45% primary residential exemption, so tax is based on 55% of a primary home's value.

Deeds are recorded with the Utah County Recorder in Provo, which charges a $40 standard fee per document plus $2 for each description over ten. Credit and debit cards carry a 2.65% processing fee, while electronic checks do not.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work in Eagle Mountain?
sections.html:
A cash sale means no mortgage underwriting, so closing depends on title work alone.

  1. Send the address and a few details about the house.
  2. We review the property and nearby sales.
  3. You accept or decline the offer.
  4. A title company prepares the paperwork and sets a closing date.
  5. The deed is recorded in Provo and you are paid at closing.

Sellers here often deal with unfinished basements, ADUs that never got a permit, or a move that has to happen quickly because of a job elsewhere. Those situations are easier to handle when no lender needs to approve the condition of the house.

faqs.q: What county is Eagle Mountain in?
faqs.a: Utah County. Eagle Mountain is in northwest Utah County, so property taxes and recording go through the county offices in Provo.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Eagle Mountain?
faqs.a: November 30. Utah County lists that date as the due date for real property taxes, and delinquent parcels are penalized beginning December 1.

faqs.q: Which school district will Eagle Mountain be in after 2027?
faqs.a: The Lake Mountain School District. It takes over from Alpine School District on July 1, 2027 and also covers Saratoga Springs, Cedar Fort and Fairfield.

faqs.q: Can I rent my Eagle Mountain basement apartment short term?
faqs.a: No, not as an ADU. Eagle Mountain requires ADU rentals to run at least 30 consecutive days, and other short-term rentals owe a 1% transient room tax.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Utah County?
faqs.a: The standard fee is $40 per document, with $2 for each additional description over ten. The Recorder will not record a document until the fees are paid or authorized electronically.
